GridPro

GridPro grid and connectivity import utilities.

Provides functions to read GridPro structured-grid text files into Block objects and to parse GridPro connectivity files into plot3d.connectivity_fast-compatible face-match dictionaries with boundary-condition grouping.

Import Functions

plot3d.gridpro.import_functions.read_gridpro_to_blocks(filename: str, encoding: str = 'utf-8', comment_prefixes: Tuple[str, ...] = ('#', '//')) → List[Block][source]

Read a structured GridPro text grid into Plot3D Block objects.

Parameters:

  • filename – Path to the GridPro grid file.

  • encoding – Encoding to use while reading the text file.

  • comment_prefixes – Line prefixes that should be treated as comments.

Raises:

ValueError – If a block does not contain the expected number of floats.

Returns:

A list of Block objects representing each GridPro block.

Return type:

List[Block]

plot3d.gridpro.import_functions.read_gridpro_connectivity(file_path: str, sb_zero_based_in_file: bool = True, index_zero_based_in_file: bool = True, inlet_ids: List[int] | Dict[str, Any] | None = None, outlet_ids: List[int] | Dict[str, Any] | None = None, wall_ids: List[int] | Dict[str, Any] | None = None, symm_slip_ids: List[int] | Dict[str, Any] | None = None, custom_bc_ids: Dict[str, List[int]] | None = None) → Dict[str, object][source]

Parse a GridPro connectivity file into plot3d.connectivity_fast-like structures.

Expected P-line layout (as provided): P pid sb1 sf1 sb2 sf2 fmap L1i L1j L1k H1i H1j H1k L2i L2j L2k H2i H2j H2k pty lbid

Boundary-condition IDs default to GridPro’s PTY values but can be overridden via the provided *_ids arguments (either a list of PTY ints or {"name": str, "ids": [...]}) or extended via custom_bc_ids={"name": [ids]}.

Parameters:

  • file_path – Path to the GridPro connectivity file.

  • sb_zero_based_in_file – Set False if sb1/sb2 are 1-based in the file.

  • index_zero_based_in_file – Set False if IMIN..KMAX are 1-based in the file.

  • inlet_ids – PTY ids to treat as inlet; defaults to [5]. Pass a dict {"name": "...", "ids": [...]} to rename the group, or provide a mapping like {"Inlet": [...], "Pressure Inlet": [...]} to emit multiple named inlet groups. Each named group remembers its base type in the returned bc_group mapping.

  • outlet_ids – PTY ids to treat as outlet; defaults to [6] (same dict options as inlet_ids).

  • wall_ids – PTY ids to treat as wall; defaults to [2] (same dict options).

  • symm_slip_ids – PTY ids to treat as symmetry/slip; defaults to [4] (same dict options).

  • custom_bc_ids – Optional mapping of group_name -> [pty ids] for any additional boundary-condition groupings (e.g., {"cooling": [500]}).

Returns:

A dictionary with keys:

  • face_matches: list of face-pair dictionaries for connected blocks.

  • all_surfaces: list of faces on the exterior (no neighbor).

  • ungrouped_surfaces: exterior faces whose PTY does not belong to any BC group.

  • bc_group: mapping of bc name to a metadata dict {"type": base_type, "pty_ids": [...], "faces": [...]}. Each face dict also includes bc_name (group label) and bc_type.

  • gif_faces: list of faces tagged as GIF (pty 12..21 or 1000).

  • periodic_faces: list of paired periodic faces (pty 3).

  • volume_zones: list describing volume zone type per superblock.

  • blocksizes: list of per-superblock cell counts (I*J*K).

  • patches: pandas DataFrame of raw patch records.

Return type:

Dict[str, object]

Examples

Basic usage with defaults:

data = read_gridpro_connectivity("connectivity.dat")
inlet_faces = data["bc_group"]["inlet"]["faces"]

Override built-in BC ids and add a custom group:

data = read_gridpro_connectivity(
    "connectivity.dat",
    inlet_ids=[5, 105],
    custom_bc_ids={"cooling_hole1": [500]},
)
cooling_faces = data["bc_group"]["cooling_hole1"]["faces"]
plot3d.gridpro.import_functions.bc_faces_by_type(bc_group: Dict[str, Any], bc_type: str, *, unique: bool = False) → List[Dict[str, int]][source]

Collect faces for a specific boundary-condition type across all named groups.

Parameters:

  • bc_group – Mapping returned by read_gridpro_connectivity() (supports both the legacy {name: [faces]} and the new {name: {"type": ..., "faces": [...]}} shapes).

  • bc_type – Base BC type ("inlet", "outlet", "wall", "symm_slip").

  • unique – When True, keep only the first face per unique id.

Returns:

List of face dictionaries belonging to the requested base type.
